reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: a computed over a list of 128, settled once per write — the walk cached
reading.floor: the same filter-and-sum called in the consumer body, no node — one read per write
reading.caveat: THE FLOOR OF WHAT A NODE CAN DO, AND THE ROW IT SHOULD LOSE. One read per write means the derive body runs exactly once on both arms, so everything the node does is overhead and nothing it holds is ever handed back. A node cannot win here and is not meant to; the row exists to price the overhead alone, so that the rows below it can be read as "what the reads bought against this" [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. IF THIS ROW COMES OUT AT OR BELOW 1.00 THE INSTRUMENT IS WRONG, not the design — there is no mechanism by which a node beats its own body at one call each. RESIDUALS. AGAINST THE NODE: it is the SHIPPED `OIMComputed`, so it is a filed slot carrying `effects`, `holdCount`, `owner` and `key`, and every read pays a call into `anySourceChangedSinceRun`, an `isRevisionAfter` per source, and — when it does run — the comparator and two pairs of stamps. The body arm allocates nothing and carries no state at all. AGAINST THE BODY ARM: nothing. It is a plain call of the same function the node derives through, and both arms write through the same `OIMChannel.write` over the same slot shape, so the write side is identical and cancels in the ratio. WHAT NEITHER ARM PAYS: the frame. No effect is subscribed and `channel.flush()` is never called. WHAT IS NOT VARIED HERE: the comparator cut. Every write moves a row that the filter keeps often enough for the derived sum to move, so the node is never handed the case where its value held and the readers below it are spared — the arrangement in which a node is at its BEST after the read count itself. It is a separate row and it is not in this file yet.

reading.ours: the same node, read eight times per write — seven reads answered from the cache
reading.floor: the same body, walked in full on all eight reads
reading.caveat: THE ARRANGEMENT PEOPLE REACH FOR A MEMO IN: a list that is expensive to walk, and more re-renders than writes. Eight reads per write is a modest ratio for a screen — a hover, a parent re-render and a sibling update all read without writing. WHAT THE ROW IS ASKING: whether seven skipped walks of 128 rows outweigh eight rounds of a node's bookkeeping. THE ANSWER IS AN ARITHMETIC ONE and the row exists to check it against a clock rather than against a count of operations. RESIDUALS. reading.ours: a computed whose body reads ONE field, read eight times per write
reading.floor: that one field read in the consumer body, eight times per write
reading.caveat: THE SAME READ RATIO AS THE ROW TWO ABOVE, WITH THE BODY MADE TRIVIAL — so the pair of rows isolates the other axis. This is `churnChain`'s derive body: one field off one row. WHAT IT DECIDES: whether a node can be worth holding for a body this cheap at a read ratio that would carry a dear one. If it cannot, then the boundary is a fact about the BODY and belongs in the documentation as one — build a node when the body walks something, not when it reads a field [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. reading.ours: build four computeds over the list, settle the head once, drop the stack
reading.floor: build one closure over the same list, call it once, drop it
reading.caveat: THE `churnChain` SHAPE, PRICED AS ITSELF. That scenario mounts a private stack of four derivations per subscriber, writes one row, reads once and unmounts — so the structure is built, used once and destroyed, and neither of the two things a node buys (a cached walk, a value shared between readers) can occur. THE ROW EXISTS TO SAY WHAT OUR NUMBER THERE IS MADE OF: four allocations, their source lists and their stamps, against one closure. A participant whose adapter builds no stack is not faster on that scenario, it is doing something else — and this row is the size of "something else" [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE: the unmount. Both arms drop their references and let the collector take them, and no `detach` is called on either side, because the body arm has nothing to detach and charging only one arm for a teardown would be the asymmetry this file exists to avoid. RESIDUALS.
